source.title: AND: Audio Network Dissection for Interpreting Deep Acoustic Models
source.authors: Tung-Yu Wu; Yu-Xiang Lin; T. Weng

record.tranche_reason: Extends neuron-level interpretation to acoustic models and reports interpretability results, but does not test the language- or vision-model versions in the claim.
record.gate_note: The study measures neuron interpretability in audio models using its own cluster-consistency criterion and reports layerwise results. Those findings are relevant to neuron interpretability but do not test the listed versions, which concern language or vision models, attribution graphs, or explanation scoring on new text. No rows are linked to a claim version. Figure-only values are retained as figure only rather than estimated.
record.test_reason: The study builds a neuron-description tool (AND) for audio transformers (AST, BEATs). It measures the share of 'uninterpretable' neurons with its own caption-clustering criterion, not by scoring explanations on held-out activations. None of its results bear on any version. V1 and V2 concern language models, V3 InceptionV1, and V4 vision models and the architecture or tools argument. V5 concerns attribution graphs. V6 and V7 concern how explanations predict activations on new inputs, and here human ratings judge descriptions only against the same top-5 activating clips. It cites Bills et al. 2023, an original source, only as related work. The record's 'discusses'/T3 is inconsistent, since T3 implies a test. The findings belong under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but incomplete. The authors conclude that AND gives accurate descriptions of acoustic neurons and supports concept-specific pruning for unlearning. They find models discriminate audio by combinations of basic acoustic features rather than high-level concepts. Their training-strategy finding is that supervised training narrows neuron attention with depth, while self-supervised learning keeps neurons polysemantic.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces an audio-specific dissection pipeline using audio captions, summaries, and clustering; it does not apply the original Qwen3 pole audit or automated neuron-explanation scoring method.
record.method_sensitivity: Interpretability percentages vary with the threshold τ and the number of highly activated samples top-K. The text reports similar broad trends under different τ and top-K settings.

fits_no_version.finding: In audio transformers on ESC50, the share of neurons failing a caption-cluster consistency test falls from shallow to deep blocks in supervised AST. It stays flat in SSL BEATs-frozen. On GTZAN the share is at most 20% at τ=4. Shares vary with τ and top-K.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In audio transformers, the share of neurons whose top-activating clips share a common description depends on layer and training strategy (supervised vs self-supervised), and on the threshold chosen.

fits_no_version.finding: The average number of acoustic adjectives per neuron narrows with depth in supervised AST (p<0.001). The trend is weaker in BEATs-finetuned and absent in BEATs-frozen (p>0.05).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Supervised training narrows the description breadth of audio neurons with depth; self-supervised pretraining does not.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235 (2024)
record.problems: The interpretability measure is defined by clustering caption sentences and a threshold τ, rather than by testing explanations on held-out activations. Many layerwise values are presented only in figures. The study concerns audio models, so its results do not directly establish the claim's language- or vision-model estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows extracted from Sections 4.3–4.4 or Table 4: those results concern concept pruning and task performance rather than the claim's listed versions or the study's direct interpretability measurements.

untested.parts: All: other language models, dense or MoE, at scale. Audio transformers are not language models.
All: InceptionV1 canonical polysemantic neurons and recursive generalization.
All. The study shows training strategy shifts its interpretability share in audio models, but does not test architecture, regularization or tool quality in vision models.
All: neuron-based attribution graphs and reconstruction error.
All: explanations are never tested on where neurons fire outside their top activating examples.
All: no simulation-based scoring of explanations on new text.

record.verdict_notes: Audio-modality neuron dissection. The interpretability criterion is internal, based on cluster overlap of captions for the top-K clips, and is threshold-dependent. Human evaluation (mean rating 3.49/5 for summaries) was done by the authors on the same activating clips used to build the descriptions.

versions.untested_parts: Qwen3-32B neuron poles and the reported one-job, two-job, and not-understood shares.
Language models, dense and mixture-of-experts models, and parameter scales up to trillions; the study examines audio models.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car examples and the recursive-generalization interpretation.
Vision-model interpretability estimates and the proposed architecture, regularization, and tool explanations.
Attribution graphs built from a large model's own neurons and reconstruction error.
Testing neuron explanations on activations not used to write them, including prediction of where a neuron fires.
Automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.
